questions.q: Breech is the m/c malpresentation with longitudinal lie and breech/podalic presentation. Match incidence – 28 wks : 34 wks : term.
M/c cause of breech overall and of recurrent breech:
opts: Prematurity (spontaneous rotation not yet occurred); uterine malformation
questions.exp: Overall prematurity; recurrent breech – uterine malformation. (Book p550)

questions.q: Match the posture – Flexed/complete breech : Frank breech : Knee presentation : Footling breech.
opts: Hips and knees flexed : hips flexed, knees extended : hips extended, knees flexed : hips and knees extended
Hips flexed, knees extended : hips and knees flexed : hips and knees extended : hips extended, knees flexed
Hips and knees extended : hips and knees flexed : hips flexed, knees extended : hips extended, knees flexed
Hips extended, knees flexed : hips flexed, knees extended : hips and knees flexed : hips and knees extended
questions.exp: Complete: hips + knees flexed; frank: hips flexed/knees extended; knee: hips extended/knees flexed; footling: both extended. (Book p550)

questions.q: Structures felt on P/V – complete breech : frank breech : knee : footling.
opts: Heel + anal opening + ischial tuberosities + external genitalia : anal opening + ischial tuberosities + genitalia : knees : feet
questions.exp: Complete: heel + anus + tuberosities + genitalia; frank: anus + tuberosities + genitalia (no heel); knee: knees; footling: feet. (Book p550)

questions.q: Occurrence – complete breech : frank breech.
opts: Least common breech overall, m/c in multigravida : m/c overall and in primigravida
M/c in primigravida : m/c in multigravida
questions.exp: Complete: least common overall, m/c in multigravida; frank: m/c overall and in primigravida. (Book p550)

questions.q: Risk of cord prolapse across breech types:
opts: Complete less, frank least (bitrochanteric 10 cm covers fully dilated cervix), knee (+), footling highest
questions.exp: Frank least (bitrochanteric 10 cm plugs the cervix), complete less, knee +, footling highest. (Book p550)

questions.q: Overall ranking of cord prolapse risk and the m/c position in breech:
opts: Transverse lie > footling breech > knee presentation; dorso-anterior
questions.exp: Cord prolapse: transverse lie > footling > knee; m/c breech position dorso-anterior. (Book p551)

questions.sec: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
questions.q: USG in breech is used to confirm diagnosis, assess type (rule out ECV C/I) and to rule out:
opts: Gross congenital anomalies (15% incidence in breech; ECV C/I) and hyperextension of neck (stargazer breech); estimate weight (ECV C/I if ≥4 kg)
questions.exp: Rule out anomalies (15%, ECV C/I), stargazer breech (hyperextended neck), estimate weight (≥4 kg C/I), check prerequisites. (Book p551)

questions.sec: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
questions.q: ECV flowchart for breech at term with no C/I (done in OPD at >37 weeks) – successful : unsuccessful : fetal distress.
opts: Send patient home (await labour) : try 2nd attempt – if successful start oxytocin/induce, if unsuccessful elective C-section at 39 wks : stop, revert to original position, emergency C-section
questions.exp: Success → home; failure → 2nd attempt (success → induce; failure → elective CS at 39 wks); distress → stop, revert, emergency CS. (Book p551)

questions.sec: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
questions.q: Modes of delivery in breech and preference:
questions.exp: C-section is strongly preferred over assisted breech delivery. (Book p551)

questions.sec: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
questions.q: Absolute indications for C-section in breech include all EXCEPT:
opts: Primigravida with breech (this is a RELATIVE indication)
Footling/knee/stargazer breech (ECV C/I) and preterm breech/weight <1.5 kg
Post-term or baby >4 kg, 1st twin breech, previous C-section
PIH/placenta previa, breech score ≤3, protracted active phase (treated as CPD)
questions.exp: Primigravida with breech is a relative indication; the others are absolute. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
questions.q: Protracted active phase (delay in 1st/2nd stage) in a breech is considered as ______ and managed by ______.
questions.exp: Delay in breech labour = CPD → immediate C-section. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites
questions.q: Assisted breech delivery – denominator : engaging diameter : m/c position.
questions.exp: Denominator sacrum; bitrochanteric 10 cm; LSA m/c. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites
questions.q: Main complication of vaginal breech delivery:
opts: Head (last part to be delivered) can get stuck → fetal hypoxic injury/intracranial haemorrhage
questions.exp: Entrapped after-coming head → hypoxia/ICH. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites
questions.q: Contraindications in assisted breech (and all malpresentations):
opts: Induction and augmentation of labour – abnormalities can rupture membranes → cord prolapse
questions.exp: IOL/augmentation avoided in all malpresentations (membrane rupture → cord prolapse). (Book p552)

questions.sec: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites
questions.q: Prerequisites for assisted breech delivery:
opts: Centre with emergency C-section facilities, senior supervision, baby <4 kg, nil oral with IV fluids, continuous CTG
Home delivery permissible, baby any weight
Junior doctor alone, no IV access
questions.exp: Emergency CS facility, senior doctor, weight <4 kg, NPO + IV fluids, continuous CTG. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks
questions.q: Mechanism of breech delivery in RSA – engagement and descent:
opts: Buttocks engage in right oblique diameter; anterior buttock touches levator ani and (Hart's rule) rotates forward and medially – buttock and sacrum rotate 1/8th of a circle
Buttocks engage in AP diameter and rotate 2/8th
Buttocks engage left oblique, no rotation
questions.exp: Engagement in right oblique; Hart's rule – part touching levator ani rotates forward/medially; 1/8th rotation. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks
questions.q: In breech, which part lies directly behind the pubic symphysis, and what is unique about the denominator?
opts: Anterior buttock; breech is the only exception where the denominator (sacrum) does not lie behind the pubic symphysis
Sacrum; denominator behind symphysis as usual
questions.exp: Anterior buttock lies behind symphysis; breech is the only presentation where the denominator (sacrum) is not behind symphysis. Buttocks then clear the perineum (± episiotomy). (Book p553)

questions.sec: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks
questions.q: When spontaneous delivery of buttocks does not occur – match manoeuvre to breech type: complete breech : frank breech.
opts: Groin traction : Pinard manoeuvre (unlocking the popliteal fossa)
questions.exp: Groin traction for complete breech; Pinard's manoeuvre (pressure in popliteal fossa to flex knee) for frank breech. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks
questions.q: The Savage technique in breech delivery:
opts: Warm moist towel wrapped around baby's lower body to prevent cord exposure (precedes shoulder delivery); touching the cord → vasospasm → fetal distress
Suprapubic pressure to flex the head
Rotation of trunk to free arms
questions.exp: Savage technique: warm moist towel around lower body to avoid cord handling (vasospasm). (Book p553)

questions.sec: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre
questions.q: Shoulder delivery in breech – the bisacromial diameter (12 cm) engages along the ______; the anterior shoulder touches levator ani and rotates ______.
opts: Right oblique diameter; anteriorly by 1/8th of a circle
questions.exp: Bisacromial 12 cm along right oblique; anterior shoulder rotates anteriorly 1/8th; anterior shoulder then posterior shoulder/arm deliver. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre
questions.q: If the shoulders are not along the AP diameter, the first step is:
opts: Hold the baby's back and turn shoulders into the AP diameter → await spontaneous delivery
questions.exp: Back held and shoulders turned into AP diameter; if spontaneous delivery fails → Lovset's. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre
questions.q: Lovset's manoeuvre involves:
opts: Fingers on baby's back rotating the trunk so the posterior shoulder becomes anterior → arm and shoulder deliver spontaneously; then anterior shoulder delivered the same way
questions.exp: Lovset's: rotate so posterior shoulder becomes anterior, deliver, repeat for other shoulder. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre
questions.q: If Lovset's manoeuvre fails:
opts: Reach the cubital fossa with two fingers and deliver the arm
Apply Piper's forceps to the arm
questions.exp: Failure of Lovset's → reach cubital fossa with 2 fingers and sweep the arm down. (Book p554)

questions.q: The after-coming head of breech is the ______ part delivered and is delivered by ______.
questions.exp: Head is the last part, delivered by flexion (opposite to vertex which delivers by extension). (Book p554)

questions.q: Burns-Marshall technique sequence:
opts: When nape of neck visible baby hangs by its own weight → suprapubic pressure (promotes neck flexion) and feet swung towards mother's abdomen → head delivered
Fingers in mouth and shoulder traction
questions.exp: Burns-Marshall: baby hangs → suprapubic pressure + feet toward maternal abdomen → head delivers. (Book p554)

questions.q: Bracht technique differs from Burns-Marshall in that:
opts: Baby is not allowed to hang
questions.exp: Bracht = Burns-Marshall without suprapubic pressure. (Book p555)

questions.q: Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit technique combines:
opts: Shoulder traction + malar flexion (fingers on malar bones, baby astride the forearm)
questions.exp: MSV = shoulder traction with malar flexion. (Book p555)

questions.q: Piper's forceps are:
opts: Long forceps – best method for delivering the after-coming head; have pelvic, cephalic and perineal/reverse pelvic curves
questions.exp: Piper's: long forceps, best for after-coming head; pelvic, cephalic and reverse pelvic (perineal) curve. (Book p555)

questions.q: Prague manoeuvre is used for delivery of the head in ______ position, where the head is delivered by ______; the m/c position is ______ (head by flexion).
questions.exp: Dorso-posterior → Prague manoeuvre (head by extension); dorso-anterior m/c (head by flexion). Head occupies opposite oblique to shoulders/buttocks. (Book p555)

questions.sec: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction
questions.q: Entrapped after-coming head – preterm breech : term breech.
opts: Dührssen's incisions on cervix at 2 and 10 o'clock → deliver head : entire body pushed back into uterus and C-section (Zavanelli technique)
questions.exp: Preterm: Dührssen's cervical incisions at 2 & 10 o'clock; term: Zavanelli (replace and C-section). (Book p555)

questions.sec: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction
questions.q: Complications of breech delivery and the m/c cause of death:
opts: Intracranial haemorrhage (m/c death), fetal asphyxia, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, abdominal injuries
questions.exp: ICH is m/c cause of death; also asphyxia, HIE, abdominal injuries. (Book p555)

questions.sec: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction
questions.q: Breech extraction is indicated in:
opts: Twin pregnancy with 1st twin cephalic and 2nd twin transverse lie
questions.exp: Indication: 2nd twin in transverse lie after vaginal delivery of cephalic 1st twin. (Book p556)

questions.sec: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction
questions.q: Method of breech extraction:
opts: Vaginal delivery of 1st twin → shift to OT → internal podalic version under GA → breech delivery under GA; all manoeuvres without maternal effort
questions.exp: After 1st twin: OT, internal podalic version under GA, breech delivery under GA, no maternal effort. (Book p556)

questions.q: Indications for instrumental delivery (with station ≥ +2):
opts: Prolonged 2nd stage, fetal distress, prophylactic shortening of 2nd stage in maternal exhaustion, heart disease, PIH
Placenta previa, cord prolapse at 4 cm
questions.exp: Prolonged 2nd stage, fetal distress, prophylactic use (exhaustion, heart disease, PIH); station ≥ +2. (Book p557)

questions.q: Prerequisites mnemonic FORCEPS – expand it:
opts: Fully dilated os; Occiput/favourable position; Rotated head + Ruptured membranes; Consent + Contracting uterus; Episiotomy + Engaged head + Empty bladder; Pelvis adequate; CPD absent
Fetus alive; Oxytocin; Rotate; Cut; Extract; Pull; Suture
Forceps; Obstetrician; Room; Consent; Epidural; Pelvis; Scissors
Full term; Occiput anterior; Rupture; Catheter; Episiotomy; Push; Stitch
questions.exp: F full dilatation, O favourable position, R rotated head/ruptured membranes, C consent/contracting uterus, E episiotomy/engaged/empty bladder, P pelvis adequate, S (CPD) absent. (Book p557)

questions.q: Favourable position for instrumental delivery:
opts: Sagittal suture in AP diameter with maximum rotation of 45° (DOA/DOP/ROA/LOA) and station ≥ +2
questions.exp: Sagittal suture AP, ≤45° rotation (DOA, DOP, ROA, LOA), station ≥ +2. (Book p557)

questions.q: Forceps vs vacuum – prerequisites differ how?
opts: Forceps need all prerequisites; vacuum can be used with incomplete cervical dilatation ≥6 cm and a non-rotated head
Vacuum needs all; forceps allow 6 cm
questions.exp: Vacuum may be applied at ≥6 cm and to an unrotated head; forceps require all prerequisites. (Book p557)

questions.q: Best-suited case for vacuum and the choice in maternal heart disease:
opts: Vertex presentation with fully dilated cervix and rotated head; heart disease → forceps (↓ maternal efforts) > vacuum
questions.exp: Vacuum ideal for vertex, full dilatation, rotated head; heart disease → forceps to reduce maternal effort. (Book p557)

questions.q: Contraindications specific to VACUUM:
opts: Preterm babies (ICH risk), intrauterine death (macerated head), after-coming head of breech, face presentation (mento-anterior)
questions.exp: Vacuum C/I: preterm, IUD, after-coming head, face presentation. (Book p558)

questions.q: Absolute contraindications to any instrumental delivery:
opts: CPD, inadequate/contracted pelvis, fetal bony deformities (osteogenesis imperfecta), fetal coagulopathy; avoided in HIV-positive women
questions.exp: Absolute: CPD, contracted pelvis, OI, fetal coagulopathy; avoid in HIV-positive. (Book p558)

questions.q: Silastic cups – advantages and pressures:
opts: Safer/less traumatic, easy to apply, bell/mushroom shaped; initial 0.2 kg/cm², maximum 0.8 kg/cm² (600 mmHg) generated in 2 min (used in fetal distress)
questions.exp: Silastic: safer, bell/mushroom; 0.2 → 0.8 kg/cm² (600 mmHg) within 2 min in fetal distress. (Book p558)

questions.q: Correct application of the vacuum cup:
opts: Centre of cup at the flexion point on sagittal suture – 6 cm posterior to anterior fontanelle / 3 cm anterior to posterior fontanelle; rim touches posterior fontanelle; cup diameter 6 cm
questions.exp: Flexion point: 6 cm behind anterior fontanelle (cup edge 3 cm), rim touches posterior fontanelle; anterior placement → extension → trauma. (Book p558)

questions.q: The Omnicup is:
opts: A newer, smaller, portable, disposable vacuum device indicated for OA and OP deliveries
A metal cup for face presentation
questions.exp: Omnicup: newer, small, portable, disposable; OA and OP deliveries. (Book p559)

questions.q: Parts of obstetric forceps include:
opts: Handles, finger guards, lock, shanks, heel, blade with window (fenestration), pelvic curve, cephalic curve
questions.exp: Handles, finger guards, lock, shanks, heel, fenestrated blade, pelvic and cephalic curves. (Book p559)

questions.q: Advantages of fenestrations (windows) in the blade:
opts: Light weight, less traumatic, ↓ risk of head compression
questions.exp: Fenestration: lighter, less traumatic, less head compression. (Book p559)

questions.q: Types of lock – English lock (m/c) : sliding lock.
opts: Two sockets (one on each handle), closes only when left blade introduced first : single socket
questions.exp: English lock: 2 sockets, left blade first; sliding lock: single socket (Kielland). (Book p559)

questions.q: Left/right forceps identification:
opts: 'Left' and 'right' are with respect to the mother; correctly held left forceps – socket faces upwards; right – socket faces downwards; pelvic curve faces upwards
With respect to the operator; both sockets up
questions.exp: Named w.r.t. mother; left blade socket up, right socket down; pelvic curve upward. (Book p560)

questions.q: Correctly applied forceps are identified by:
opts: Lock closes properly and both blades equidistant from the sagittal suture (applied along occipito-mental diameter)
questions.exp: Lock closes; blades equidistant from sagittal suture; along occipito-mental diameter. (Book p560)

questions.q: Wrigley forceps:
opts: Outlet forceps; short and light; total length 27.5 cm, shank 2.5 cm
questions.exp: Wrigley: outlet, short, light, 27.5 cm total, 2.5 cm shank. (Book p560)

questions.q: Kielland forceps:
opts: Long, the only forceps that can rotate the fetal head (rotation forceps), sliding lock; outdated
Short outlet forceps with English lock
questions.exp: Kielland: long, rotational, sliding lock, outdated. (Book p560)

questions.q: Match – Piper's forceps : Tucker-McLane forceps.
opts: Longest forceps (English lock) for after-coming head of breech : only forceps with a solid blade
questions.exp: Piper's – longest, English lock, after-coming head; Tucker-McLane – solid blade. (Book p560)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Low forceps (m/c type) vs outlet (Wrigley) forceps criteria:
opts: Low: station ≥ +2 without touching perineum; outlet: head at perineum, scalp visible at introitus, skull at pelvic floor, sagittal suture in AP (ideal)
questions.exp: Low ≥ +2 not touching perineum; outlet: head at perineum, scalp visible, skull on pelvic floor, sagittal suture AP. (Book p561)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Mid-cavity forceps (0/+1 station) and high forceps (−ve station) are:
questions.exp: Mid-cavity and high forceps are obsolete. (Book p561)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Direction of pull – ideal position and basis; low forceps pulls : outlet forceps pulls.
opts: Lithotomy, based on maternal abdomen; low: downward+backward → downward → downward+forward : outlet: downward → downward+forward
Supine; low: upward → forward : outlet: backward
Left lateral; low: forward only : outlet: downward only
questions.exp: Lithotomy; directions relative to maternal abdomen. Low: down+back, down, down+forward. Outlet: down, down+forward. (Book p561)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Prior to forceps delivery:
questions.exp: Consent, epidural/pudendal analgesia, episiotomy. (Book p561)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Traction force for forceps – primigravida : multigravida.
questions.exp: Primi 16–18 kg; multi 12–13 kg. (Book p562)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: M/c complication – forceps : vacuum; ease of use:
opts: Maternal injury : fetal injury; forceps require more training, vacuum easier (m/c used)
Fetal injury : maternal injury; vacuum harder
questions.exp: Forceps → maternal injury; vacuum → fetal injury; vacuum easier and m/c used. (Book p562)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Fetal complications – forceps : vacuum.
opts: Facial (VII) nerve palsy, brachial plexus injury, corneal injury : VI nerve palsy, shoulder dystocia, cephalhematoma, subgaleal haemorrhage, retinal injury
VI nerve palsy : VII nerve palsy
questions.exp: Forceps: VII palsy, brachial plexus, corneal injury. Vacuum: VI palsy, shoulder dystocia, cephalhematoma, subgaleal bleed, retinal injury. (Book p562)

questions.sec: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
questions.q: Failed forceps/vacuum is defined as ______ and managed by ______.
opts: 3 unsuccessful trials to deliver the head; C-section
questions.exp: 3 unsuccessful attempts = failed instrumental delivery → C-section. (Book p562)

units.title: Breech: features, incidence, causes & types
units.guide: Track breech incidence by gestation, its m/c causes, and distinguish complete, frank, knee and footling breech by posture, P/V findings and cord-prolapse risk. Focus for this checkpoint: Breech: features, incidence, causes & types.

units.title: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery
units.guide: Use USG to screen for ECV, follow the ECV flowchart, and apply the absolute and relative indications for caesarean section. Focus for this checkpoint: Management of breech: USG, ECV & mode of delivery.

units.title: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites
units.guide: Know the denominator, engaging diameter and m/c position of breech, the deadly complication of the after-coming head, and the safety prerequisites. Focus for this checkpoint: Assisted breech delivery: features, complication, C/I & prerequisites.

units.title: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks
units.guide: Follow the RSA mechanism from oblique engagement to spontaneous buttock delivery, and apply groin traction, Pinard's manoeuvre and the Savage technique. Focus for this checkpoint: Mechanism of breech delivery & manoeuvres for buttocks.

units.title: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre
units.guide: Trace the bisacromial diameter through the pelvis and rescue extended arms with Lovset's manoeuvre or cubital fossa delivery. Focus for this checkpoint: Shoulder delivery in breech & Lovset's manoeuvre.

units.title: After-coming head of breech: manoeuvres
units.guide: Deliver the after-coming head with Burns-Marshall, Bracht, Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit, Piper's forceps and Prague manoeuvre – and know when each applies. Focus for this checkpoint: After-coming head of breech: manoeuvres.

units.title: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction
units.guide: Manage the entrapped head differently in preterm and term breech, recall the m/c cause of death, and define breech extraction for the second twin. Focus for this checkpoint: Complications of breech delivery & breech extraction.

units.title: Instrumental delivery: indications, prerequisites & choice
units.guide: Learn the indications, the FORCEPS mnemonic of prerequisites, the favourable positions, and when vacuum can replace forceps. Focus for this checkpoint: Instrumental delivery: indications, prerequisites & choice.

units.title: Contraindications & vacuum delivery technique
units.guide: Recall the vacuum-specific and absolute contraindications, then set up the silastic cup pressures and the flexion-point application. Focus for this checkpoint: Contraindications & vacuum delivery technique.

units.title: Forceps: parts, locks, handedness & types
units.guide: Name the parts of the obstetric forceps, the two lock types, how to identify left from right, and the four classic forceps with their unique features. Focus for this checkpoint: Forceps: parts, locks, handedness & types.

units.title: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications
units.guide: Classify low vs outlet forceps, pull in the correct sequence of directions, quote traction forces, and compare complications of forceps and vacuum. Focus for this checkpoint: Forceps application, direction of pull & complications.
